title: Regional Health Insurer — On‑Prem Pilot SOW & Runbook (draft)
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working SOW + operations runbook for a 12-week on-prem pilot with Regional Health Insurer (RHI). Goal: validate Redwood Private deployment in customer datacenter behind their firewall, demonstrate HIPAA-safe ingestion and extraction for claim triage assistant, and produce a repeatable runbook the RHI infra team can operate post-pilot.

Important notes (working):
- This draft is intentionally lean; focus on what we can reliably deliver in 12 weeks with a 2-node GPU footprint.
- Primary stakeholder at RHI: Emily Santos (Director, Automation). Security lead: Omar Farooq.
- Dependencies: onsite rack space + network ACLs, customer KMS creds, access window for initial install (2 business days), agreed test data subset (de-identified).

Objectives (success criteria):
1) Deployed Redwood Private control plane + inference nodes in RHI staging VPC or air-gapped rack.
2) End-to-end demo: ingest de-identified claims, run triage model, return structured triage outcome with <800ms p95 inference latency for short prompts, and throughput 50 reqs/min sustained.
3) Security/compliance: all data at rest encrypted (customer KMS), audit logs forwarded to RHI ELK, and access controls verified by RHI security team.
4) Knowledge transfer: ops runbook + 2 half-day workshops for RHI SREs and App team.

Scope (in-scope):
- Redwood responsibilities:
  - Provide Private package (control plane container images + on-prem runtime) and installation support (remote + 2 onsite engineer-days if requested).
  - Basic integration with customer KMS (Key wrap for model weights + tenant data).
  - Model onboarding: deploy one open-weight triage model (quantized variant) and a smaller backup model for graceful fallback.
  - Implement KV/prefix cache for high-cardinality prompts to demonstrate cost/latency gains.
  - Deliver runbook, rollback checklist, and handoff training sessions.

- Customer responsibilities:
  - Provide VM/GPU nodes (NVIDIA A10/A30 or better) and networking (NAT, ACLs for control plane communication), cluster admin.
  - Provide de-identified sample dataset and KMS access in test environment.
  - Assign engineer(s) for weekly syncs and participate in training.

Out-of-scope (for pilot):
- Full production rollout, SLA guarantees beyond pilot timeframe.
- Custom model re-training or PII-heavy data ingestion without prior legal sign-off.
- Multi-region high-availability; pilot is single-site.

Deliverables:
- Deployment artifacts: helm manifests, Ansible playbooks, or installation script (preferred option noted during install prep).
- Runtime config: batching/caching profile tuned to claim triage workload.
- Security config: KMS integration guide, audit log pipeline config, default RBAC roles.
- Workshops: 2x half-day sessions (runbook & ops, model/feature tuning) + ops handoff doc.
- Post-pilot report: performance numbers, cost estimates for 3 capacity options, recommended next steps.

High-level timeline (12 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): finalize SOW, NDA updates, sign MSA addendum for private.
- Week 1: install window scheduling, infra validation (networking, KMS).
- Week 2: control plane bootstrap + node provisioning.
- Week 3: baseline model deploy, smoke tests.
- Weeks 4–6: workload tuning, caching, latency optimization.
- Week 7: security review and audit pipeline validation.
- Week 8: canary testing with live de-identified samples.
- Week 9: first workshop (ops/runbook).
- Week 10: resilience tests, failover/fallback validation.
- Week 11: second workshop (model ops & quality monitoring).
- Week 12: final report and wrap, recommended next steps.

Milestones & acceptance:
- Milestone A: infra validated and control plane online (acceptance by RHI infra).
- Milestone B: demo of end-to-end triage on sample set with performance targets met.
- Milestone C: runbook delivered and training completed.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Redwood AE (engaged): Diego Martinez — SOW owner, primary contact.
- Redwood SEs: Aisha Patel (install lead), Marcus Chen (runtime tuning), Hannah Lee (security/compliance).
- Customer: Emily Santos (project sponsor), Omar Farooq (security review), RHI SREs for day-to-day ops.

Security and compliance checklist (pilot-level):
- KMS integration for secret keys and model encryption: test key-access flows, rotate keys in test window.
- Audit logging: ensure inference request logs and admin events are sent to RHI ELK; sampling enabled for PII-sensitive endpoints.
- Network: restrict control plane egress to allowed Redwood control IPs (if required), and validate no public S3 endpoints used for protected data.
- Data minimization: only de-identified test data allowed during pilot; any PII ingestion requires explicit approvals.

Operational runbook highlights (short):
- Install checklist: kernel drivers, docker/CRI versions, nvidia toolkit, kernel parameter tweaks, ulimits.
- Start/stop sequence: control-plane first, then worker nodes, kv cache warm-up step.
- Routine maintenance: nightly cache compaction, weekly model health check, monthly OS patches (maintenance window template attached).
- Troubleshooting: common failure modes with quick fixes (GPU OOM → reduce batch size, drift in latency → reset cache + restart router).

Workshop agenda (half-day ops):
- 30m: architecture walkthrough + design rationale.
- 45m: hands-on deploy (control plane bring-up).
- 30m: runtime tuning demo (batch/caching knobs).
- 30m: security walk-through (KMS & audit logs).
- 15m: open Q&A + next steps.

Pricing & rate card (pilot-level):
- Fixed professional services fee: $85,000 (covers up to 12 weeks, includes 10 eng-days onsite or equivalent remote time, runbook, and workshops).
- Optional add-ons:
  - Additional onsite days: $3,500/day.
  - Extended run support (30 days post-pilot): $12,000.
  - Production readiness package (capacity planning + HA setup): $45,000 estimate (separate SOW).
- Hardware note: RHI responsible for compute; Redwood can provide sizing guidance.

Assumptions and risks:
- Assumes access to at least 2x A10-class GPUs; performance claims tied to that baseline.
- Risk: delayed KMS onboarding will push install window. Contingency: we can run a local test KMS for validation in Week 2 but not for security sign-off.
- Risk: customer IT change freeze windows — plan install slots early.

Acceptance criteria for billing triggers:
- 30% invoice on SOW signature (mobilization), 40% on Milestone B acceptance, 30% on final report delivery.

Appendix / quick links (working):
- Ticket references: JIRA-SS-4678 (install), JIRA-SS-4680 (k8s config), JIRA-SEC-112 (KMS integration).
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-REG-INS-ONPREM-1 (pilot runbook canonical).
- Template: ops-checklist-template.docx (internal template).

Open items / TODOs (tracked):
- [ ] Confirm onsite dates and travel approval windows with RHI PM (Emily).
- [ ] Get test KMS credentials and scope of key rotation policy from Omar.
- [ ] Finalize batch/caching profile after initial 48-hour run — Marcus to own.
- [ ] Legal review: MSA addendum for private deployment (Claire, Legal).

Notes to self / quick comms log:
- 2024-11-05 DM: RHI asked about offline model updates; propose signed artifact exchange + rsync over secure channel.
- 2024-11-09 AH: security team requested that audit logs be hashed before forwarding — check retention policy with RHI.

End of draft.
Please add comments in-line for any missing items; I'll incorporate into next revision before customer review on 2024-11-20.
